seo.title: Rent the Runway: AI-personalized discovery - +11% favorites and +129% views (2026)
seo.meta_description: Personalized carousels and a For You feed live for all subscribers since April 2026, plus AI-generated product imagery: +11% hearting, +129% views.
seo.resume_citable: Rent the Runway made its personalized carousels and For You feed live for all subscribers in April 2026, with an 11% increase in hearting, while AI-generated product imagery pushed views on the affected styles up 129% (Q1 FY2026 results, revenue $89.9M).

faq.q: What did Rent the Runway deploy in terms of AI for discovery?
faq.a: Personalized carousels and a For You feed live for all subscribers since April 2026, tuned to their favorites and tastes, plus AI-generated product imagery to refresh old inventory. The automated generation of complete outfits was still in internal testing.

faq.q: What results does the brand publish?
faq.a: An 11% increase in hearting on the home page for active subscribers and a 129% increase in views on the styles switched to AI imagery, in the Q1 FY2026 results (revenue $89.9M, +29.2% year-over-year, 155,692 active subscribers).

pattern: personalization of the discovery journey (carousels and For You feed) plus AI-generated product imagery on old inventory
objectif_business: Deepen discovery and engagement for active subscribers of the subscription rental service, so they find pieces to rent faster, book more, and stay subscribed. Rent the Runway describes a discovery engine at the core of its 2026 strategy, with add-on revenue up 70.4% year-over-year, driven by stronger subscriber engagement.
points_cles: Personalized carousels and For You feed live for all subscribers since April 2026.
Recommendation engine on first-party signals plus AI-generated product imagery (stack not disclosed).
Hearting +11% on the home page, views +129% on styles with AI imagery.
description: In April 2026, Rent the Runway deployed personalized carousels across its platform, live for all subscribers. The subscriber discovers pieces close to her recent favorites and browses a For You feed tuned to her tastes. The brand measures an 11% increase in hearting (favoriting) on the home page for active subscribers. Second component, also in April 2026, AI-generated product imagery replaced old visuals with more realistic images meant to help the customer picture herself in the piece; views on these styles increased 129%. A third workstream, the automated generation of complete outfits, entered internal testing in May 2026 and was not yet open to subscribers as of the results date: Rent the Runway indicates it intends to deploy it in the following months, which makes it a future extension rather than a result at scale. The credibility context is a public quarter (Q1 FY2026, closed April 30, 2026, published June 3, 2026) with revenue of 89.9 million dollars, up 29.2% year-over-year, and 155,692 active subscribers at period end. Rent the Runway discloses neither the models nor the providers behind these features.

resultats.metrique: Home-page hearting (active subscribers), after the carousels and the For You feed
Views on styles, after switching to more realistic AI imagery
Personalized carousels live for all subscribers since April 2026 (end of Q1 FY2026)

niveau_preuve.justification: Figures published by Rent the Runway itself in its 8-K filed with the SEC (Exhibit 99.1, Q1 FY2026 results, T1 primary), reproduced identically in its official release and concordant with the earnings call transcript. The +11% hearting and +129% views are explicitly attributed by the brand to the two AI features, and the carousels are declared live for all subscribers. Primary financial-results document, hence level A.

fonctionnement_operationnel.cadence: Personalized feed recomputed continuously as the subscriber browses and favorites; product imagery regenerated in batches when inventory is updated or refreshed
fonctionnement_operationnel.opere_par: Rent the Runway's product and data team (provider and models not disclosed)
fonctionnement_operationnel.signal_pilote: The subscriber's first-party engagement signals: favorites (hearts), views, rental history. The For You feed optimizes on these; if these signals are missing or thin for a new subscriber, personalization falls back on generic recommendations.

etapes.detail: The subscriber favorites pieces, views listings, rents; these events feed her taste profile.
The recommendation engine composes the personalized carousels and the feed from recent favorites and detected preferences.
An AI imagery model produces more realistic visuals to replace old inventory images, to help the customer picture herself.

etapes.etape: Delivery on the site and app
etapes.detail: Carousels, For You feed, and new visuals are served on the home page and product listings of all subscribers.
The team tracks hearting, views, and engagement to validate impact and extend the scope (internal testing of outfit generation ahead of a future deployment).

prerequis_data: Per-user first-party engagement history (favorites, views, purchases or rentals)
Structured product catalog with style attributes usable by a recommendation engine
Product image inventory, with identification of old or underperforming visuals to regenerate
prerequis_orga: Product and data team able to operate a recommendation engine over time
Governance on AI-generated imagery: brand consistency, quality control, transparency on synthetic content
GDPR legal basis for personalization and, in the EU, AI Act marking of generated visuals
stack_possible: Recommendation engine (item-to-item and personalized feed) on first-party data
Model for generating or improving product images
Delivery layer on home page and product listings with A/B testing
Engagement instrumentation (favorites, views) to measure impact
replication.premiere_etape: Cleanly instrument first-party engagement signals (favorites, views, conversions) and launch a first item-to-item personalized carousel on the home page, in an A/B test, before tackling generated imagery.

playbook.action: Audit and make reliable the collection of per-user first-party engagement signals (favorites, views, rentals or purchases).
playbook.livrable: Usable per-user taste profile, the basis of personalization.

playbook.action: Deploy a first personalized carousel and a discovery feed tuned to recent favorites, in an A/B test on the home page.
playbook.livrable: Personalized carousel measured against a non-personalized feed.

playbook.action: Identify products whose imagery is old or underperforming, then regenerate realistic AI visuals with quality control and brand consistency.
playbook.livrable: Batch of renewed product images, with before/after view tracking.

playbook.action: Extend delivery to the whole base once impact is validated, keeping the engagement instrumentation.
playbook.livrable: Personalization live for all users, impact tracked.

playbook.action: Explore the generation of complete outfits in internal testing before any opening, to move from the isolated piece to the look.

replication.equipe: 1 product team (PM, design) + data scientists or ML engineers for the recommendation engine and generated imagery + a merchandising or brand function to validate visual consistency.

statut_vivant.note: Personalized carousels declared live for all subscribers in the June 3, 2026 results, with AI-driven discovery set as a central axis of the 2026 strategy. Recent deployment (about three months as of the verification date): to re-monitor next quarter. Outfit generation remained in internal testing, not open to subscribers.

transposable_ue.note: The mechanism relies on first-party engagement data (favorites, views, rental history) to personalize a discovery feed, which transposes to a GDPR environment with a clear legal basis and a right to object. The second component, AI-generated product imagery, falls under the transparency obligations on synthetic content provided by the AI Act (marking of AI-generated visuals). The detail of the stack is not disclosed by Rent the Runway, so the orchestration would have to be rebuilt.
